questions.prompt: A detector reports an object centre at pixel (410, 260) and nothing else. What does that pixel determine about its 3-D position?
options: Only a ray from the camera centre; every depth along it gives the same pixel
A unique 3-D point, once the intrinsics are known and the image is undistorted
The lateral position but not the height, since only the x coordinate is fixed
The depth but not the direction, since the pixel measures only distance
questions.explanation: Intrinsics turn a pixel into a direction (x, y, 1); depth is a separate unknown.

questions.prompt: fx = fy = 600, cx = 320, cy = 240. Project the camera-frame point (0.3, 0.1, 3.0) m. Give u in pixels (precision 0.1).
A 0.20 m wide board facing the camera is 50 pixels wide; fx = 750. What is its distance in metres? (precision 0.01)
A 1920-pixel-wide image has fx = 1400 px. What is the horizontal field of view in degrees? (precision 0.1)
questions.skillLabel: Field of view and focal length

questions.prompt: Your projection function returns (270, 240) for the camera-frame point (0.2, 0, -2) with f=500, c=(320,240). What should a correct implementation do?
options: Return the pixel, since the point is just left of the image centre
Clamp the pixel to the nearest border of the image
Reject the point because it is behind the camera (Z <= 0)
Take the absolute value of Z and then project as usual
questions.explanation: Negative Z flips the signs, producing a mirrored pixel for an invisible point.

questions.prompt: A 8 mm lens on a sensor 6.4 mm wide produces 1600-pixel-wide images. Give the focal length in pixels. (precision 1)
questions.skillLabel: Field of view and focal length

questions.prompt: You double the focal length of a camera that stays in place. Explain what changes in the image (size, field of view) and what does not (perspective: the ratio of near and far object sizes). What would change the ratio?
rubric: Image offsets from the principal point and object sizes double; field of view narrows.
Ratio of sizes depends only on depths, so zooming leaves it unchanged.
Moving the camera changes the depths and therefore the ratio.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
